name: showreel-c3-grey-text

voice.text: Grey on beige. Nobody can read it. Turns out, text needs contrast. Fix one: darken the words. Fix two: a lighter board. Fix three: check the ratio. Four and a half to one. Same board, now readable.

caption:
Grey on beige looks soft. Nobody can read it. ☕

1. Darken the words. Contrast is the difference in brightness between text and what's behind it.
2. A lighter board. Pull the background the other way and the gap grows from both sides.
3. Check the ratio. Aim for at least 4.5 to 1 for normal text (WCAG); a free contrast checker gives the number in seconds.

Save this for your next menu, slide or sign. Which soft colour combo have you seen that nobody could read?

edges_ok.why: the design-tutorial stage (a café specials board on a counter) fills the frame by design
